candidates.reason: Contois kinetics makes specific growth depend on substrate relative to biomass, a useful test given the markedly different starting biomass concentrations across experiments.
Monod kinetics is a simple saturation baseline for glucose-limited growth, consistent with the very low measured glucose in E1 and E2.
Andrews kinetics adds substrate inhibition to saturation; it can test whether growth is suppressed as glucose accumulates to high levels in E3.

answer.note: No statistical-agent feedback is available yet, so these choices span biomass-dependent limitation, ordinary saturation, and substrate inhibition.
